problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(0,{\sigma }^{2})$ is a normal random variable with $P(|X|<3)=0.6046,$ use the table to find $\sigma ,$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.7\,$ | $\,0.7734\,$ | $\,0.7764\,$ | $\,0.7794\,$ |
| $\,0.8\,$ | $\,0.8023\,$ | $\,0.8051\,$ | $\,0.8078\,$ |
| $\,0.9\,$ | $\,0.8289\,$ | $\,0.8315\,$ | $\,0.8340\,$ |

$\sigma ≈$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
First, we express the given probability as

$$
P(|X|<3)=P(-3<X<3).
$$

Then, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-3<X<3) & =0.6046 \\ 2P(0<X<3) & =0.6046 \\ P(0<X<3) & =0.3023 \\ P(X<3)-P(X<0) & =0.3023 \\ P(X<3)-0.5 & =0.3023 \\ P(X<3) & =0.8023 \\ P(X\le 3) & =0.8023\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 3) & =0.8023 \\ P(Z\le \frac{3-0}{\sigma }) & =0.8023 \\ Φ(\frac{3}{\sigma }) & =0.8023 \\ \frac{3}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.8023)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.85)=0.8023\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.8023)=0.85.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{\sigma } & =0.85 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{3}{0.85} \\ \sigma  & ≈3.53.\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
